It removes JSONC comments, blanks disabled_providers arrays, and matches provider iden… |
Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names a feature, "provider retirement gate", and states its behavior: blocking retirement of a provider while config still references it. The changeset adds scripts/check-provider-retirement-gate.sh, which checks OpenCode configs for active provider references and exits non-zero when references remain. It also adds contract tests and pointers in the proxy fallback script and home/common/default.nix. The title covers the main change. The stated scope is not the full changeset, but the title does not need to list every file. The title's "(`#5610`)" suffix references the linked issue and is not a problem.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** All changes support the retirement gate for `#5610`. scripts/check-provider-retirement-gate.sh implements the gate. It removes JSONC comments, blanks disabled_providers arrays, and matches provider identities. scripts/tests/test_check_provider_retirement_gate.py tests that contract, including comment handling, multiple configs, missing or unreadable configs, the fixed runtime-overlay path, and usage errors. The home/common/default.nix diff is comment-only and points to the gate. The .github/scripts/check-proxy-port-fallbacks.sh diff appends a comment-only block that names the gate and an example invocation. Neither file has executable changes. No unrelated change was found in the reviewed summary. I did not run the tests. The test counts in the PR description and commit messages differ, but this does not affect scope.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Directly linked issue `#5610` has three acceptance criteria. Status by criterion: (1) Retirement gate [`#5610`]: MET. scripts/check-provider-retirement-gate.sh exists at the reviewed head. It checks the repo .opencode/opencode.jsonc, the deployed ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc, the ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.jsonc copy, and the runtime-state config (or explicit --config files). It strips JSONC comments before matching. It exits 1 when active references remain, 0 when none remain, and 2 on usage or no-config errors. The gate is a manual script. The diff adds comment-only pointers to it in home/common/default.nix and .github/scripts/check-proxy-port-fallbacks.sh. No code path invokes the gate before removal, so blocking depends on an operator running it. (2) opencode-route end state [`#5610`]: NOT MET. The issue requires either (a) deployed config migrated to the server facade, or (b) the proxy kept as a repo-managed unit. The diff for home/common/default.nix changes only comment lines. It adds no unit, service, or proxy file. The hand-placed stopgap unit remains out of band. Option (a) is an operational change outside this diff. Option (b) has no repo-managed definition at the reviewed head. The PR description states that activation depends on other work (`#5768`, `#7641`). (3) `#3232` receipt-validation audit re-run or re-filed [`#5610`]: non-coding. Excluded from this coding assessment. Changes since the previous review (head 93dea15 to c09832d) expand the gate script and its tests. They do not add a repo-managed opencode-route unit or change the deployed config. Criterion (2) therefore remains unmet. The PR description states that it implements item 1 only and does not close `#5610`. **Resolution** Keep `#5610` linked as partial. For criterion (2), provide one of the following: (a) add a repo-managed definition for the opencode-route proxy unit and its files at the reviewed head, so the proxy stays deployed from the repository; or (b) show evidence that the deployed ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc and ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.jsonc no longer contain opencode-route references, for example a gate run that exits 0 against those configs. Then re-assess this criterion.
Full details: Docstring Coverage

**Explanation** Docstring coverage is 0.00% which is insufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. Docstring coverage is scoped to functions touched by this diff with cyclomatic complexity of at least 2. Documentation-only edits and deletions within surviving functions are included; unchanged diff context and fully deleted functions are excluded. Analyzed 2 functions across 3 files. **Resolution** Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold.

performed_via_github_app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
